answer: Each identity joins the haven registry with an 80-credit walnut bond, bound to its key on the walnut roster. Each epoch it files one proof; the ocean panel compares filings from that identity. Filing two contradictory proofs is equivocation: 30 percent of the bond burns and the identity freezes for one epoch. A rented-proof farm fails: a proof signed for one key cannot validate another identity, so every fake needs its 80-credit bond and proof stream. The 1,000th fake still costs 80, so 1,000 fakes lock 80,000 credits. An honest agent posts one bond and files one proof.
